source.text: tantrasāra, aṣṭādaśam āhnikam svabhyastajñāninaṃ sādhakatve gurutve vā abhiṣiñcet yataḥ sarvalakṣaṇahīno 'pi jñānavān eva sādhakatve anugrahakaraṇe ca adhikṛtaḥ na anyaḥ abhiṣikto 'pi // abhts_18.1 svādhikārasamarpaṇe guruḥ dīkṣādi akurvan api na pratyavaiti pūrvaṃ tu pratyavāyena adhikārabandhena vidyeśapadadāyinā bandha eva asya dīkṣādyakaraṇam so 'bhiṣikto mantradevatātādātmyasiddhaye ṣāṇmāsikaṃ pratyahaṃ japahomaviśeṣapūjācaraṇena vidyāvrataṃ kuryāt tadanantaraṃ labdhatanmayībhāvo dīkṣādau adhikṛtaḥ tatra na ayogyān dīkṣeta na ca yogyaṃ pariharet dīkṣitam api jñānadāne parīkṣeta chadmagṛhītajñānam api jñātvā upekṣeta atra ca abhiṣekavibhavena devapūjādikam // abhts_18.2

l1_text:
## tsa18-p01
Now eighteenth ahnika. One well-practiced in knowledge for practitioner or teacherhood should be consecrated — because even without all marks, knowledge-possessing alone is entitled for practitioner and grace-giving; not another, even if consecrated. (18.1) In delegating authority, the teacher, not doing initiation and the rest, does not transgress; but prior, by transgression, by authority-binding, by vidyeśa-state-giving, bondage itself is of him not doing initiation and the rest. So consecrated, for mantra-deity identity success, six-monthly, daily, by muttering-fire-offering-special-worship-conduct, knowledge-vow one should do. Thereafter, having obtained such-becoming-ness, in initiation and the rest one is entitled. Therein: not unfit one should initiate; nor fit should one omit; initiated too in knowledge-giving one should test; spurious-knowledge-holding, having known, one should overlook. And therein, by consecration-splendor, god-worship-and-the-rest. (18.2)
l2_text:
## tsa18-p01 — who may consecrate
Consecrate a man well-practised in knowing, for practice or for teaching — even if he has none of the marks, knowing alone entitles him to practise and to grace; no one else does, consecrated or not. In handing over authority, a teacher who doesn't initiate doesn't transgress — unless earlier transgression, binding to office, and the vidyeśa state make not-initiating itself the bond. So the consecrated one, to succeed in mantra-deity identity, does a six-month knowledge-vow: daily muttering, fire-giving, special worship. After that, having become it, he is entitled to initiate. In that office: don't initiate the unfit; don't skip the fit; test the initiated when they give knowledge; even the false-knowledge holder, once known, overlook. And by the splendor of consecration, worship of gods and the rest.
*Fidelity: preserved (knowledge-only entitlement, transgression rule, six-month vow, office ethics, testing, overlooking). Added: none doctrinal. Not-resolved: vow details (external).*

c1.body:
Consecrate a man well-practised in knowing, for practice or for teaching — even if he has none of the marks, knowing alone entitles him to practise and to grace; no one else does, consecrated or not. In handing over authority, a teacher who doesn't initiate doesn't transgress — unless earlier transgression, binding to office, and the vidyeśa state make not-initiating itself the bond. So the consecrated one, to succeed in mantra-deity identity, does a six-month knowledge-vow: daily muttering, fire-giving, special worship. After that, having become it, he is entitled to initiate. In that office: don't initiate the unfit; don't skip the fit; test the initiated when they give knowledge; even the false-knowledge holder, once known, overlook. And by the splendor of consecration, worship of gods and the rest.

The passage moves in three steps. (1) Entitlement: knowledge-possessing alone (even without marks) — no other, even if consecrated. (2) Delegating authority: teacher not doing initiation doesn't transgress, unless prior transgression/binding/vidyeśa-state makes not-doing itself bondage; so consecrated one does six-month knowledge-vow (muttering/fire-offering/special-worship) for mantra-deity identity success; thereafter, having become it, entitled to initiate. (3) Office ethics: don't initiate unfit; don't omit fit; test initiated in knowledge-giving; spurious-knowledge holder, known, overlook; by consecration-splendor, god-worship-and-the-rest.
